published_statement: p.8: 'Our recommended solar photospheric elemental abundances are listed in Table 1, which also provides the corresponding meteoritic values for CI chondrites ... log eps_X = log(N_X/N_H) + 12.' Table 1 caption (p.42): 'Element abundances in the present-day solar photosphere. Also given are the corresponding values for CI carbonaceous chondrites (Lodders, Palme & Gail 2009). Indirect photospheric estimates have been used for the noble gases (Sect. 3.9).' Rows used by the tree include H 12.00 / 8.22+-0.04; He [10.93+-0.01] / 1.29; Li 1.05+-0.10 / 3.26+-0.05; N 7.83+-0.05 / 6.26; Ne [7.93+-0.10] / -1.12; P 5.41+-0.03 / 5.43+-0.04; Ar [6.40+-0.13] / -0.50; K 5.03+-0.09 / 5.08+-0.02; Ta -- / -0.12+-0.04; U -- / -0.54+-0.03. p.24 (sec 4.1): meteoritic scale 'renormalized ... such that the meteoritic and photospheric Si abundances agree ... log eps_X = 1.51 + log N_X.' p.10: 'The solar Li depletion cannot be explained by standard models based on the mixing length theory of convection but requires additional mixing below the convection zone.' p.23 (sec 3.11): 'the bulk composition of the Sun is higher by 0.05 dex for helium and 0.04 dex for the heavier elements ... uncertainty ... about 0.01 dex.' p.24 (sec 3.12): present-day X = 0.7381, Y = 0.2485, Z = 0.0134.
published_hypotheses: H1 present-day solar photosphere (and by extension the convection zone, p.23), not bulk/protosolar; bulk = +0.05 dex He, +0.04 dex heavier elements (sec 3.11, p.23)

H2 photospheric values inferred through a 3D hydrodynamical model atmosphere (Trampedach et al. 2009) with non-LTE 'whenever possible' (p.8); P explicitly without any non-LTE study: 'No non-LTE investigation has been performed to date for these high-excitation P i lines' (p.15)
H3 quoted 1-sigma uncertainties are part of the result: Li +-0.10, P +-0.03, K +-0.09 (K 'line-to-line scatter is disappointingly large', p.15)

H4 noble gases (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, bracketed) are INDIRECT estimates: He from helioseismology (Basu & Antia 2004), Ne from a coronal Ne/O ratio 0.175+-0.031 (Young 2005b), Ar similarly (sec 3.9, p.20)

H5 meteoritic column = CI chondrites (Lodders, Palme & Gail 2009), volatile-depleted ('not possible to rely on meteorites to determine the primordial solar system abundances' for H, He, C, N, O, Ne, p.3), pegged to photospheric Si = 7.51 (p.24)

H6 Li is depleted in the photosphere by nuclear burning via mixing below the convection zone that standard models do not produce (p.10); Li is the one non-volatile element whose photospheric value is far below meteoritic (p.25)
H7 the table describes the Sun; comparison with other stars/ISM requires diffusion (0.04 dex) and Galactic chemical enrichment (0.05-0.15 dex) corrections (sec 4.2 p.25, p.30)

lacked_data: What A09 lacked (their own words, READ): (a) any non-LTE study for P ('No non-LTE investigation has been performed to date', p.15) -- first supplied by Andrievsky & Korotin 2026 and applied in AG26 as -0.07 dex (P 5.35); (b) 3D non-LTE Li with complete UV background line opacity -- supplied by Wang et al. 2021, Li 0.96 (AAG21, AG26); (c) Genesis solar-wind Ne and Ar (AAG21 8.06, 6.38; A09 used a coronal Ne/O ratio); (d) 3D non-LTE K (AAG21 5.07 vs 5.03 with 'disappointingly large' scatter). DOES HAVING THEM CHANGE THE CONCLUSION? Evidence FOR M's hypothesis: the tree's binder identity 'P binds against a stellar photosphere' flips to Li on AAG21's data, on C11 and (by 0.6 %) on L25, and survives only by 1.7 % on AG26; the margin falls from 0.037 dex (A09) to 0.007 dex (AG26) or reverses by 0.053 dex (AAG21). Evidence AGAINST over-reading it: (i) A09's measurement is not shown wrong -- its quoted Li +- 0.10 already covers every later value and already gives a 36 % chance that Li binds; the later data moved inside A09's stated error; (ii) the magnitude (1.9e3-2.2e3 kg of photospheric stock per kg of human; 134-154 t per 70 kg), the site-selection reading, 'a chondrite beats a star' and 'not a barrier' do not move on any compilation read here; (iii) the CNO/metallicity dispute that dominates the post-2009 literature is irrelevant to the Li-P criterion, which is normalisation-free. So the authors lacked data that matters for exactly one conclusion the tree draws (which element binds), and that conclusion was never determined by A09's data in the first place.
grade_evidence: The measurement as transcribed STANDS: all 63 photospheric and 61 of 63 meteoritic values equal Table 1 (Ne, Ar meteoritic omitted -- a transcription discrepancy that moves no figure), and every tree fixture (P 1910.87, Li 0.91758, K 2.9317, stock.py 1910.5, P/Li 1.022e5, Li 2.21 dex) is reproduced from Table 1. What rests on it and MOVES with a datum that has moved and is contested: the binder identity carried into D25 (ledger.py:671-683) and stock.py:65-67 -- P under A09 (0.9176) and AG26 (0.9832), Li under AAG21 (1.1289), C11 (1.0781) and L25 (1.0061); exact criterion log eps(Li) - log eps(P) < -4.3974; P(Li binds) = 0.36 under A09's own errors. Magnitude robust (1.9e3-2.2e3). Secondary narrowings recorded, none refuting A09: 'stellar / gas giant' is the present-day Sun only (gas giant Li unburned: Li/P 0.0057, binder unchanged); 'largest gap in the table' is true only as largest photospheric deficit; 'convective envelope reaches 2.5 MK' contradicts A09 p.10 and AG26 p.52 on mechanism; 'protosolar / meteoritic' is CI rock, and the printed Li 1.0846e1 is not what the tree's own function returns (0.06821). Not WRONG: nothing here refutes A09; a transcription omission and mis-stated mechanism are discrepancies.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS for the binder identity: a consensus solar Li - P > -4.3974 dex with an error small against the margin (e.g. a 3D non-LTE centre-to-limb Li analysis confirming approx 1.05 and P non-LTE confirming approx 5.41), or the tree reporting the binder as 'P or Li, undetermined at current precision' with the magnitude as the result -- then the claim as used would stand on any compilation. To NARROWED only: restricting 'stellar photosphere' to 'present-day solar photosphere' and dropping the gas-giant Li. Toward WRONG (for the tree's claim, not A09): a converged compilation with Li - P below -4.3974 by more than its error would make 'P binds' a refuted datum-level claim.
